title: Score a detector: IoU, NMS, average precision, and Dice
brief: Write a pairwise box IoU, greedy non-maximum suppression, a matcher that labels detections as hits or misses, average precision, pixel IoU and Dice, and a soft Dice loss with its gradient.
hints: Boxes are (x1, y1, x2, y2). Use a[:, None, :] and b[None, :, :] to line up every pair, so that np.maximum of the top-left corners has shape (N, M, 2).
The overlap width is min(x2) - max(x1) and the height is min(y2) - max(y1). Clamp each at 0 before you multiply. For boxes [0,0,2,2] and [5,5,7,7], both raw widths are -3, and their product is +9.
The union is area_a + area_b - intersection. [0,0,4,4] against [2,2,6,6] has intersection 4 and union 28, so the IoU is 1/7.
For NMS, sort by descending score, then walk down the list. A box survives only when its IoU with every box in the keep list is at most thr. Never compare against a box that was suppressed.
In the worked NMS example, box 1 (score 0.8) overlaps box 0 with IoU 0.538 and is suppressed. Box 2 overlaps box 1 with IoU 0.538 but box 0 with only 0.25, so it survives.

In match_detections, a detection may only claim a ground-truth box of its own image that no earlier detection has claimed. Among those, take the one with the largest IoU, and call the detection a hit when that IoU is at least thr.
Precision after k detections is (hits so far) / k, and recall is (hits so far) / n_gt. Both come from np.cumsum of the hit flags.

For all-point AP, pad recall with 0 in front and 1 at the end, pad precision with 0 at both ends, then replace each precision by the largest precision at or to the right of it: np.maximum.accumulate on the reversed array. Add up (change in recall) * (envelope precision) over the places where recall changes. The hand example gives 1/3 + 1/3 + 0.6/3.
Dice is 2 |A and B| / (|A| + |B|), and Dice = 2 IoU / (1 + IoU). For the soft loss, with num = 2 sum(p g) + eps and den = sum(p) + sum(g) + eps, the loss is 1 - num/den.

The derivative of num/den with respect to p_i is (2 g_i den - num) / den**2. The loss gradient is its negative. With p = [0.9, 0.8, 0.2, 0.1], g = [1, 1, 0, 0], and eps = 0, it is [-0.2875, -0.2875, 0.2125, 0.2125].
